app.title: qPCR Model Fitting with MAK2+
app.summary: A person loads raw amplification curves from a qPCR instrument, along with an optional plate metadata file. They choose which wells to fit, set how much of each curve around the steepest point is used, and pick how starting amounts are turned into copy numbers. A batch run fits a mechanistic amplification model to every well. It skips wells with no signal, stamps each fit pass or fail, and fills a results table. The person then checks calibration and replicate statistics and opens individual fits. At the end they download a multi-sheet spreadsheet of per-well starting amounts, Ct values and copy numbers.

task.text: Fit a mechanistic amplification model to every well of a qPCR plate to estimate each well's starting template amount, and convert it to absolute copy numbers with a quality verdict per well.

data.text: Fluorescence readings per cycle for each well of a qPCR run, from vendor export formats, with optional per-well metadata: sample names, task (standard or unknown), known quantities and instrument thresholds.
data.item: a well's amplification curve: fluorescence over thermal cycles in one dye channel

stage.text: quantifying raw instrument amplification curves into per-well template amounts, before downstream comparison

mechanism.text: A sidebar holds the data input, fit-window and calibration settings, which drive a batch fit. The results show up as a formatted table with summary metrics, followed by calibration curves, replicate statistics tabs and a selector that opens any one well's fitted curve over its raw data.

field.text: mechanistic qPCR curve fitting for absolute quantification in molecular biology

workflow.name: fit a model to each curve in a batch and convert the fitted values to calibrated amounts

steps.here: Pick an example dataset, upload a CSV or Excel file in one of several instrument formats, enter data by hand, or reload previous results. An optional plate metadata CSV adds sample names, standards and thresholds.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Choose the wells, targets or dye channels to fit, then press 'Ready to Fit Selected Samples'.

Sliders set the first cycle to fit and how many cycles before and after the steepest point to use. A radio picks the calibration method: auto-detected standards, limited dilution, a manual factor, single-copy D0, or none.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: 'Batch Fit All Samples' triages out wells with no signal, fits the model to each remaining well, retries weak fits using channel priors, and applies pass/fail quality gates.

Group wells into replicates by a name pattern or by hand, optionally as a dilution series with groups left out. Tabs show mean, SD and CV, overlaid replicate curves, the precision of D0 against Ct, and dilution linearity.
Select any well to see its raw fluorescence with the fitted curve and its pass/fail status. Skipped wells can also be viewed.
Download a multi-sheet .xlsx containing batch results, settings, replicate and dilution sheets and native standard-curve charts, or a CSV.

distinctive: Each well's starting amount comes from fitting a mechanistic primer-depletion kinetic model. Ct comes from threshold crossing.
The fit window is cut around the cycle of maximum slope, so late-plateau artefacts are left out.
Wells are classified by quality gates (R² floor, window width, sigmoid versus linear, inflection, plateau overshoot), and wells with no signal are triaged before fitting.
Starting amounts become copy numbers through several calibration routes, including on-plate standards and a limited-dilution Poisson panel.
Interrupted batches can be resumed from a checkpoint saved after each well.
